_README: The pinned ffmpeg that ships in the Windows installer, so game recordings
(Tracker > record) come out as a compressed mp4 with sound on a PC with
nothing installed, instead of a huge silent raw AVI.
This file is TRACKED; the unpack it describes (utility/ffmpeg/) is NOT --
.gitignore excludes it. Any build machine reproduces the unpack with:
python tools/build/fetch_ffmpeg.py
which downloads `url` (BtbN's release asset), refuses anything whose
sha256 is not `sha256`, unpacks it, applies `trim`, and writes
utility/ffmpeg/.fetch-receipt.json.
WHY A GPL BUILD: recordings encode with libx264 (backend/tracker/replays/
watch_mods.py, backend/tracker/video/combo_video/), which only GPL builds
carry. Mac and Linux do not bundle one yet -- there
backend/core/media_tools.py falls back to PATH.
WHY BtbN: every input of this build is public and pinned by one commit of
github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds, so its complete source is available
upstream (the recipe pins each library's source and commit in scripts.d).
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md links that, the same way it links Blender's source.

license.holder: the FFmpeg developers and the authors of the libraries linked into it; Windows build by BtbN's FFmpeg-Builds
license.license_file: LICENSE.txt (FFmpeg's COPYING.GPLv3, which the recipe copies for gpl variants)
source_offer: Like Blender: the notice links the upstream source. FFmpeg at
`ffmpeg_source`; every library linked into the binary is pinned by
source URL and commit in the recipe's scripts.d at `recipe.commit`,
which rebuilds this exact binary with `recipe.command`.
why_unmodified: ffmpeg ships as an UNMODIFIED upstream binary invoked as a separate
process. Mere aggregation, same posture as the bundled Blender and wit.
Trimming below deletes whole files; it never patches a binary.

_README: ffplay is a player nothing calls. Nothing calls ffprobe either: a
recording's length comes from the game or its audio dump
(tracker/replays/recording.py). Each is a ~165 MB static exe.
doc/ is HTML documentation and presets/ libvpx presets nothing uses.
